audit.why: 48.05% over 308 games and the chart is nearly all Skill, with Camille taking level 1 and 2+ items. The prose is more decisive than the chart — it says Urgot owns the very early game and reclaims the lane past first item — but the shape is honest for a lane where neither champion gets a free stage.

Levels 3-5 as Camille's hit-and-run window and first item as Urgot's takeover are both right. Fear Beyond Death is 100s at rank 1 down to 70s and Disdain is 16s at rank 1 down to 14s — the second one matters most, because 'bait his E flip first' is the matchup's core instruction and it needs a number.
audit.corrected: Disdain's 16s and Fear Beyond Death's 100s written in.

audit.whatIsWrong: Urgot's passive is never named and is repeatedly conflated with his W: 'his W shotgun-leg autos', 'W Purge legs plus passive percent-HP', 'His W passive plus first-item DPS'. Two separate claims of percent-max-health damage are attached to abilities that do not have it. Camille's R is written without its article and Disdain and Corrosive Charge are only 'his E flip' and 'his Q'.
audit.why: Riot's text: Echoing Flames is the passive — 'Urgot's basic attacks and Purge periodically trigger blasts of flame from his legs, dealing physical damage'. Purge (W) is the channel that also triggers Echoing Flames. So the legs are the passive and Purge is what feeds them; writing 'W passive' merges two abilities into one and leaves the reader unable to track either. Nothing in Urgot's kit carries percent-maximum-health damage in Riot's data — Echoing Flames is flat physical — so 'his passive percent-HP grinds you down' asserts a scaling that is not there and pushes the reader toward the wrong defensive item. Disdain also shields Urgot as he charges, which is why trading into his engage is worse than it looks, and that is unstated.
audit.corrected: Echoing Flames named as the passive and Purge as the channel that triggers it; the percent-max-health claims removed rather than replaced; Disdain's self-shield stated; Corrosive Charge, Disdain and Fear Beyond Death named with their cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Bait his E flip first, then E-in on its cooldown' names the single most important cooldown in the lane without a duration.
audit.why: Disdain is 16/15.5/15/14.5/14s against Hookshot's 16/15/14/13/12s. They are almost exactly paired at rank 1 and Camille's pulls ahead as she ranks it — so the bait genuinely works, but only barely, and only if she has not spent her own E first. That arithmetic is the matchup.
audit.corrected: Both cooldowns written into wants.you[1] and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[2] says Urgot can 'finish you through your one-instance passive shield', and early repeats that Adaptive Defenses 'only soaks one instance'.
audit.why: Riot's text for Adaptive Defenses: basic attacks on champions grant a shield against their damage type for a brief duration. It is a duration shield, not a single-instance absorb, and it is granted by Camille's own attack landing rather than existing in advance. Against Purge — a continuous channel — the difference decides whether stepping in is survivable, so the wrong model here is actively harmful.
audit.corrected: Restated as a short-duration shield that only exists after her own attack lands.

edits.before: Urgot owns the very early game here — his Q Corrosive Charge drops a slow zone on your last-hit spot and his W shotgun-leg autos chip you before your E grapple is even available, so you have no all-in tool at Level 1. Don't walk up into his Q cast to last-hit; farm from max auto range on the back foot instead. Your passive shield only soaks one instance and his W keeps firing legs, so don't bait it into a sustained exchange where his percent-HP grinds you down.
edits.after: Urgot owns the very early game — Corrosive Charge drops a slow zone on your last-hit spot and Echoing Flames blasts off every auto, all before Hookshot is even available, so you have no all-in tool at Level 1. Don't walk into the Q cast to last-hit; farm from max auto range instead. Adaptive Defenses only exists once your own attack lands and it expires fast, so it cannot cover a Purge channel — never bait it into a sustained exchange.

edits.before: Levels 3 to 5 are your real opening — walk up with Q empowered, land the second Q hit for the true-damage burst, then E off a wall and dash out before his W Purge legs ramp. The trap is his E flip: it interrupts your E dash and pins you in his Q slow zone, so bait it out before you commit. Level 6 is your one stage to flip this lane — Hextech Ultimatum locks him in a 1v1 arena so his E can't reposition you and his team can't peel, letting your W max-HP damage and Q burst win clean.
edits.after: Levels 3 to 5 are your real opening — walk up with Q empowered, land the delayed second hit for the true-damage burst, then E off a wall and leave before Purge ramps Echoing Flames. The trap is Disdain: it shields him as he charges, catches you, and hurls you into the Corrosive Charge slow, so bait its 16s before you commit — your Hookshot outranges it as you rank up. At 6 The Hextech Ultimatum isolates him and his team can't peel, letting your W and Q burst win clean.

notes: Two claims of percent-maximum-health damage were attached to Urgot's passive; Riot's text for Echoing Flames is flat physical damage from leg blasts and no ability in his kit carries a percentHealth flag. I removed the claims rather than substituting a number I cannot verify. The passive/W conflation ('W shotgun legs', 'W passive percent-HP') was systematic — Echoing Flames is the passive, Purge is the channel that triggers it. Also corrected the description of Camille's own passive: it was called a 'one-instance' shield twice, but Riot describes a short-duration shield granted after her attack lands, which is a materially different thing to have against a continuous channel like Purge.
